title: GitHub Issue Auto-Linking in PR Workflow

content.title: GitHub Issue Auto-Linking in PR Workflow
content.summary: The dispatch workflow (grill → seed → tasks → export-tasks-gh → build-code → gxpush) creates GitHub issues and PRs as separate, unlinked artifacts. Merging a PR does not auto-close the corresponding GitHub issue. The fix wires three layers: build-code reads export_url from the task JSON, encodes the issue number as a gh-N segment in the branch name, and sets GITHUB_CLOSES env var before calling gxpush. gxpush then appends 'Closes #N' to the PR body — using whichever signal it finds first. This mirrors the existing Linear ticket pattern, where the ticket is encoded in the branch name and extracted by gxpush/pr-desc at PR creation time.
content.problem_statement: PRs created by the build-code/gxpush workflow do not reference their corresponding GitHub issues. Merging a PR therefore does not auto-close the linked issue. The root cause is that export_url (written back to the task JSON by export-tasks-gh after issue creation) is never read by build-code or gxpush — so the issue number is absent from the branch name and the PR body.
content.solution: Wire export_url through the build pipeline in two parallel paths (belt and suspenders): (1) build-code encodes the issue number as gh-N in the branch name and (2) sets GITHUB_CLOSES env var. gxpush checks $GITHUB_CLOSES and also applies a regex over the branch name for self-discovery. When either signal is present, gxpush appends 'Closes #N' to the PR body. If export_url is null, both paths are silently skipped.
decisions: Discovery uses both branch name encoding (gh-N segment) AND GITHUB_CLOSES env var — belt and suspenders, same pattern as Linear ticket linking.
Closing keyword injection lives in gxpush: after pr-desc generates the PR body, gxpush appends 'Closes #N'. The pr-desc script is not changed.
Branch name format encodes the GitHub issue number as a gh- prefix segment: feat/t-0023-gh-42-bootstrap-auth.
No schema changes to task-schema.json. export_url is used as-is — for the sapien GitHub repo it is always the GitHub issue URL.
Silent skip when export_url is null — build-code skips branch encoding and GITHUB_CLOSES; gxpush creates the PR without an issue link. No warning emitted.
Logic lives in build-code SKILL.md: read export_url from task JSON, extract issue number, encode gh-N in branch name, set GITHUB_CLOSES env var before calling gxpush.
branching-strategy.md is updated to document the gh-N segment in the branch name format.
gxpush is updated to (a) extract gh-[0-9]+ from the branch name via regex and (b) check $GITHUB_CLOSES env var, then append 'Closes #N' to PR_BODY when either is present.
implementation_decisions: build-code reads task JSON at runtime to obtain export_url — no new schema field or write-back needed.
gxpush regex target: gh-[0-9]+ in the branch name. GITHUB_CLOSES env var is the explicit path; branch regex is the self-discovery fallback.
content.next_action: Run /to-tasks to break this into implementation tasks for build-code SKILL.md, gxpush, and branching-strategy.md.

tasks.title: Update gxpush to append Closes #N to PR body
tasks.description: Extend gxpush to link PRs to GitHub issues by appending 'Closes #N' to PR_BODY before calling gh pr create. Two signals are checked in order: (1) $GITHUB_CLOSES env var (explicit path — expects a bare issue number like '42'), and (2) a regex extraction of gh-[0-9]+ from the branch name (self-discovery fallback). When either signal yields a number, append '\n\nCloses #N' to PR_BODY. When neither is present, skip silently — no warning, no change to PR body. The env var takes precedence when both are present.
acceptance_criteria: When GITHUB_CLOSES=42 is set, the PR body contains 'Closes #42' on a new line
When the branch name contains gh-42, the PR body contains 'Closes #42' on a new line
When both signals are present, GITHUB_CLOSES takes precedence
When neither signal is present, PR body is unchanged from pr-desc output
Shell test or manual smoke test: run gxpush --dry-run (or equivalent) with each signal combination and verify PR_BODY contents
tasks.summary: Extended gxpush to append 'Closes #N' to PR_BODY before gh pr create: checks $GITHUB_CLOSES env var first, falls back to extracting gh-[0-9]+ from branch slug, skips silently when neither is present. Added a standalone bash test script with 7 tests (10 assertions) covering all signal combinations.

tasks.title: Wire build-code SKILL.md and branching-strategy.md to encode gh-N
tasks.description: Update build-code SKILL.md and branching-strategy.md so the AI encodes the GitHub issue number in the branch name and sets GITHUB_CLOSES before calling gxpush. In SKILL.md: when processing a task, read export_url from the task JSON. If export_url is non-null and matches a GitHub issue URL, extract the issue number (last path segment of the URL). Encode it as a gh-N segment in the branch name immediately after the task ID segment (e.g. feat/t-0023-gh-42-bootstrap-auth). Set GITHUB_CLOSES=N in the shell environment before calling gxpush. If export_url is null or absent, skip both steps silently. In branching-strategy.md: document the optional gh-N segment and its position in the branch name format.
acceptance_criteria: build-code SKILL.md documents the export_url read, issue number extraction, gh-N branch encoding, and GITHUB_CLOSES env var steps
build-code SKILL.md documents the silent-skip behavior when export_url is null
branching-strategy.md shows the gh-N segment in the branch name format (e.g. {prefix}/t-{id}-gh-{issue}-{slug})
End-to-end smoke test: run build-code against a task whose export_url is set to a GitHub issue URL and confirm the created branch contains gh-N and the PR body contains 'Closes #N'
tasks.summary: Updated build-code SKILL.md step 4c to read export_url from the task object, extract the GitHub issue number when the URL matches a GitHub issue pattern, encode it as gh-N in the branch name after the task-ID segment, and set GITHUB_CLOSES=N before gxpush runs. Updated branching-strategy.md to document the optional gh-N segment with examples.
